This tornado developed over extreme southwest Lipscomb County at 1656 CST and then moved northeast for about one mile before dissipating at 1657 CST. Although the tornado remained over open county...it did cause damage to a barn. No injuries were reported.

This tornado developed over open country six miles southwest of Darrouzett at 1839 CST and traveled northeast. The tornado dissipated at 1845 CST about four miles southwest of Darrouzett. No damage or injuries were reported.

This tornado developed over open country about three miles southwest of Lipscomb at 2155 CST. The tornado traveled northeast for about four miles damaging a farm and trees. The tornado dissipated at 2205 CST just northwest of Lipscomb. No injuries were reported.

From the mesonet station located near Lipscomb.

This tornado developed to the west of Highway 1453. It resulted in a few downed tree branches before crossing into Ellis County, Oklahoma. This tornado was also observed by several storm spotters and chasers.
The first 60 mph plus wind gust was measured at 76 mph at 1927CDT. The mesonet then quickly measured a 95 and 96 mph wind gust over the next two minute. The last wind gust of 61 mph was at 1935CDT.
This mesonet first measured a wind gust of 59 mph at 2352CDT, with another gust of 65 mph at 2353CDT.
Hail up to quarter size fell along County Road X.
A swath of large hail fell from two miles west of Darrouzett to four miles southeast of Darrouzett. Hail ranged from half dollar size to two inches in diameter.
Baseball size hail fell west of Follett. This resulted in broken windshields o some vehicles in the area.

Lipscomb 8W mesonet station measured a 68 mph wind gust from a collapsing thunderstorm.

A supercell thunderstorm moved across the eastern part of Lipscomb County. It produced hail up to the size of golfballs from roughly seven miles southeast of Lipscomb to Higgins. Quarter size hail fell about seven miles to the northeast of Glazier.

Large hail fell northwest of Higgins. Hail sizes were mostly dime size to quarter size, but a few hailstones were slightly larger than a golf ball. This resulted in damage to a fire engine that was en route to a wildfire caused by lightning.
